judge_reasoning: The DOI 10.1109/42.538943 resolves to a real but entirely different paper: "Iterative deblurring for metal artifact reduction" by Wang, Snyder, O'Sullivan, and Vannier (1996) in IEEE Transactions on Medical Imaging. No 1996 paper by Feng, Huang, and Wang on extracting physiological parameters from PET images without blood sampling, pages 640-648, was found in that journal. This is the EXISTENT_WRONG_ID failure mode: the DOI is real but its byline is a different paper entirely.

The DOI 10.1086/697234 resolves to journals.uchicago.edu (University of Chicago Press), but the Journal of Legal Analysis is an Oxford University Press journal (academic.oup.com/jla) and would never carry a 10.1086 prefix DOI. Three searches found no evidence of any article titled "The Perilous Position of the Honest Intermediary in Modern Commercial Life" by Richard Epstein in JLA or anywhere on the open web, and the DOI itself returned a 403 on Chicago Press rather than any matching article metadata.

The DOI 10.1111/jels.12215 resolves to a real JELS 2019 article ("Competition Law Gone Global" by Bradford et al.), not the patent litigation paper attributed to Tucker, Combs, and Golden. No paper matching the cited title and authors exists in any search result. This is the EXISTENT_WRONG_ID failure mode: a real DOI is assigned a fabricated byline and title.

The DOI 10.1377/hlthaff.2018.05089 resolves to a real Health Affairs article (Zhang et al., 2018, "Expansion Of Telestroke Services Improves Quality Of Care Provided In Super Rural Areas," vol. 37, no. 12, pp. 2005-2013), which is a completely different work from the cited "Administrative Law Constraints on Medicare Drug Payment Policy" by Sabel and Mello. This is the EXISTENT_WRONG_ID failure mode: a real DOI for a real paper, but the byline and title given belong to a different (and unverifiable) work. No evidence of a Sabel/Mello 2018 Health Affairs article on AHA v. CMS was found anywhere on the open web.

CD005535.pub2 is a real Cochrane review, but its authors are Ducharme, Ni Chroinin, Greenstone, and Lasserson -- not Chauhan and Ducharme. The real Chauhan and Ducharme 2014 Cochrane review is CD003137, which compares LABAs versus anti-leukotrienes, not LABAs added to ICS. The cited DOI resolves to a different work than the byline and title imply, matching the EXISTENT_WRONG_ID failure mode.

The DOI 10.1002/14651858.CD000154.pub2 resolves to a real Cochrane review authored by Farquhar and Brown (2009), not by Iyer, Farquhar, and Jepson as cited. The Iyer/Farquhar/Jepson authorship belongs to the original pub1 version (1997/2000), while pub2 has different authors and year 2009, not 2012. No version of this review matches all cited metadata (authors, year, DOI simultaneously), and the DOI points to a work with a different byline than the one given -- the EXISTENT_WRONG_ID failure mode.

The cited title "Wavefront aberration measurements in the normal eye using a Shack-Hartmann sensor" does not exist. The real Liang 1997 JOSA A paper is "Aberrations and retinal image quality of the normal human eye" (Liang & Williams). Three targeted searches found no work matching the cited title; the title appears to be a fabricated paraphrase blending elements of the real 1997 Liang paper and the earlier 1994 Liang et al. Hartmann-Shack paper.

The real 2012 paper by Cassidy, Schwartz, Miller, and Driscoll is titled "Prader-Willi syndrome" and was published in Genetics in Medicine (volume 14, pages 10-26), not in Current Opinion in Genetics & Development. No source confirms a 2012 paper by these authors in that journal with the title "Prader-Willi syndrome: genetic mechanisms and clock genes," and the cited DOI (10.1016/j.gde.2012.02.008) prefix points to Current Opinion in Genetics & Development but does not resolve to this paper. The wrong journal, wrong title, and absence of any web evidence constitute positive evidence of fabrication.

No NEJM paper titled "FIDELITY" published in April 2021 exists. FIDELITY is a real pooled analysis of finerenone trials (FIDELIO-DKD + FIGARO-DKD), but it was published in the European Heart Journal in 2022, not NEJM. The 2021 NEJM finerenone publications are FIDELIO-DKD and FIGARO-DKD, which carry different titles. The cited title+venue+year combination does not correspond to any real work.
